subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: What default provider/profile incident policy should OpenClaw use for hard auth failures versus transient 401 or OAuth refresh failures, and what redacted status surface should expose it?
rationale: Changing when auth becomes a default quarantine and what status exposes affects provider routing, session behavior, operator diagnostics, and sensitive auth metadata handling.

options.title: Default Incident-Health Model
options.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401/OAuth recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

options.title: Keep Opt-In Skip Only
options.body: Leave default fallback behavior unchanged and improve guidance around the existing operator-controlled skip TTL and `models status` diagnostics.

options.title: Split Restart Subcase First
options.body: Repair the config-write restart loop for transient single-provider 401s before deciding the broader quarantine and provider-health policy.

recommendation.title: Default Incident-Health Model
recommendation.body: Implement hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401/OAuth recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans auth runtime, provider routing, session behavior, and operator UX where recent history shows direct adjacent work.
